title: Legal and regulatory requirements
text: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.
vendor_question: Which AI-specific legal and regulatory regimes have you assessed your product against, and where is that assessment documented?
source: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), Core — GOVERN 1.1

title: AI system inventory
text: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to organizational risk priorities.
vendor_question: Do you maintain an inventory of the AI systems and models embedded in your product, and can you share its scope?
source: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), Core — GOVERN 1.6

title: Testing, incident identification, information sharing
text: Organizational practices are in place to enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing.
vendor_question: What is your process for identifying and disclosing AI-related incidents to customers, and what is the notification window?
source: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), Core — GOVERN 4.3

title: Third-party AI risk policies
text: Policies and procedures are in place that address AI risks associated with third-party entities, including risks of infringement of a third-party's intellectual property or other rights.
vendor_question: Which third-party model providers do you rely on, and what governance do you apply to them?
source: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), Core — GOVERN 6.1

title: Tasks and methods defined
text: The specific tasks and methods used to implement the tasks that the AI system will support are defined (e.g., classifiers, generative models, recommenders).
vendor_question: Which specific AI capabilities are in the product, and what model type implements each?
source: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), Core — MAP 2.1

title: Knowledge limits and human oversight of output
text: Information about the AI system's knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans is documented.
vendor_question: Where do you document the model's known limitations and the intended human review of its output?
source: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), Core — MAP 2.2

title: Human oversight processes
text: Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies from the govern function.
vendor_question: What human oversight is built into AI-driven decisions, and can a customer configure or escalate it?
source: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), Core — MAP 3.5

title: Security and resilience evaluated
text: AI system security and resilience – as identified in the map function – are evaluated and documented.
vendor_question: Have you tested the AI features specifically for prompt injection, model extraction, and adversarial input, and is that testing documented?
source: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), Core — MEASURE 2.7

title: Privacy risk examined
text: Privacy risk of the AI system – as identified in the map function – is examined and documented.
vendor_question: Is customer data used to train or fine-tune models, what is the retention period, and how does a customer opt out?
source: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), Core — MEASURE 2.10

title: Fairness and bias evaluated
text: Fairness and bias – as identified in the map function – are evaluated and results are documented.
vendor_question: Have you evaluated the AI features for bias across affected populations, and can you share the results?
source: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), Core — MEASURE 2.11

title: Pre-trained model monitoring
text: Pre-trained models which are used for development are monitored as part of AI system regular monitoring and maintenance.
vendor_question: How do you monitor the third-party pre-trained models you depend on, and how are customers notified when one changes?
source: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), Core — MANAGE 3.2

title: Incident communication and recovery
text: Incidents and errors are communicated to relevant AI actors, including affected communities. Processes for tracking, responding to, and recovering from incidents and errors are followed and documented.
vendor_question: What is your documented process for tracking, responding to, and recovering from AI-related incidents?
source: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), Core — MANAGE 4.3
